market_holds: No usable option chain (sealed baseline: ATM legs not two-sided, unusable_chain), so there is no implied move. My own arithmetic on Yahoo daily bars gives the last five prints' moves as open/close vs the prior close: Nov-26-2025 -4.2/-8.0, Mar-5-2026 +2.5/-8.7, Jun-2-2026 -5.7/-10.4, Aug-27-2026 +6.9/+5.2, Aug-27-2025 -2.2/+3.8. That is a usual move of about 5-10%, 3 of the last 4 down by the close, and opens that often faded into the session. Run-up: -13.2% over 5 days and -19.3% over 20 days (baseline). The stock was $2.40 on Nov-18 and $2.06 on Nov-24. It fell -5.0% on Nov-19 and -9.6% on Nov-20, when peer Youdao reported Q3 learning services -5.2% and blamed summer enrolments shifting into Q2, which also widened its Q3 cash outflow. KWEB fell about 4% and FXI about 3% over the same days. So part of the drop is China beta and part looks like a read-through from Youdao. Consensus (Yahoo analysis page, fetched 2026-11-24): Q3 revenue RMB1.91B from 1 analyst (+21% YoY, 2.8% above the top of the RMB1.838-1.858B guide); Q4 RMB1.99B from 1 analyst (+18%); FY2026 RMB7.07B from 4 analysts (+15%, matching management's old ~15% FY target). The FY figure only adds up if Q4 grows about 7%, so the estimates are stale and do not agree with each other. FY2026 non-GAAP EPS consensus is positive at 0.14 (range 0.10-0.22), even though H1 had a non-GAAP net loss of RMB87.6M and Q3 has historically been a loss quarter. The company has beaten the top of its own revenue guide by 2.3-5.7% in each of the last three quarters. Short interest is low (about 2.0M shares, 3.7 days to cover, Oct-30 per a search snippet). A buyback is ongoing (36.5M ADSs cumulative as of Aug-26-2026).
view: Q3 revenue is close to known. Management guided on Aug-27, two months into a quarter whose summer classes were mostly delivered, and it has cleared the top of its guide by 2-6% for three quarters. A print of about RMB1.90-1.95B is likely, which is in line with or slightly above the single RMB1.91B estimate, so the headline will not move the stock. The reaction will turn on three things. First, the Q4 guide: Gaotu guides conservatively, and a mid-teens guide of about RMB1.90-1.97B would sit below the lone RMB1.99B Q4 estimate but above what the stale FY consensus implies. Second, Q3 cash flow and billings: last year a RMB660M Q3 operating outflow and a decelerating guide sent the stock -8%, and Youdao's comment that summer sales moved into Q2 points to a wide Q3 outflow again. Gaotu's own Q2 operating cash inflow rose 46%, which is consistent with that. Third, profitability: FY consensus EPS is positive, but the H1 loss plus a seasonal Q3 loss make a full-year profit unlikely. Q2 showed the stock can rise on a revenue beat despite an EPS miss. Against that, the stock has already fallen 14% in five sessions on the Youdao read-through and China beta, so some of the cash-flow and deceleration fear is in the price, and the buyback gives support. The evidence pulls both ways and I cannot show the price is behind on either side. The base rate of selling off after prints (3 of the last 4) is balanced by the fresh de-rating. Slight lean down, no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: Q3 revenue is near-certain to land at or above the guide, but consensus (RMB1.91B) already expects that. The reaction will turn on the Q4 guide, Q3 cash flow and profitability, and the evidence on those points both ways. The 14% drop into the print on Youdao's read-through and China weakness already holds some of the downside I can identify. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide at or above about +18% (RMB1.99B or more) together with a narrower Q3 operating cash outflow than last year's RMB660M would make me lean long. A Q4 guide in single digits, or management dropping the FY2026 net-profit aim, would make me lean short.

self_critique: The case for long is real. Gaotu has beaten the top of its guide three quarters running. The stock fell 14% in a week on a peer's company-specific weakness and China beta rather than on Gaotu news. Its Q2 call showed strong new-enrolment billings (+55% in 1-on-1). A day-before-Thanksgiving tape with low short interest and an active buyback could carry a clean beat and a mid-teens Q4 guide to a relief bounce of several percent. The case for short is that the stock has closed down after three of the last four prints for exactly the reasons likely again this time: a decelerating guide against a +21% comp and seasonal cash outflow. Both cases are about as strong, which is why I stay near 50.
